facts.statement: A Polish-Mongolian expedition discovered a small dinosaur fossil at Bayn Dzak, Mongolia, in 1965.
facts.quote: In 1965, a Polish-Mongolian paleontological expedition found a fossil of a small dinosaur at Bayn Dzak, Mongolia.

facts.statement: Elzanowski and Wellnhofer named the type species Archaeornithoides deinosauriscus in 1992.
facts.quote: The remains were named as the type species Archaeornithoides deinosauriscus by Elzanowski and Peter Wellnhofer in 1992.

facts.statement: Archaeornithoides was a maniraptoran theropod dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Archaeornithoides is a genus of maniraptoran theropod dinosaur of the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Archaeornithoides had an estimated body length of fifty to sixty centimeters, making it one of the smallest known non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The body length was estimated at fifty to sixty centimetres, making the Archaeornithoides type one of the smallest known non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Archaeornithoides bears at least eight small, conical, and smooth teeth that lack serrations.
facts.quote: The maxilla bears at least eight teeth. These are small, conical and smooth, lacking wrinkles, serrations or carinae.

facts.statement: Some researchers noted that the specimen may have passed through the digestive tract of a predator before fossilization.
facts.quote: Clark and colleagues (2002) noted that it may have also passed through the digestive tract of the predator before fossilization.

facts.statement: Adult Archaeornithoides is estimated to have reached a length of one meter, weighed approximately two kilograms, and was omnivorous.
facts.quote: La longitud cuando adulto es incierta aunque se estima que medía 1 metro de longitud, omnívoro, su peso era aproximadamente de 2 kilogramos

facts.statement: Bever and Norell (2009) found no evidence supporting a close relationship between Archaeornithoides and Avialae and only weak support for it being a juvenile troodontid.
facts.quote: Bever and Norell (in 2009) found no evidence to support the placement of Archaeornithoides close to Avialae, and only weak support for the idea that it is a juvenile troodontid.

facts.statement: Archaeornithoides is classified tentatively within the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: familia: Troodontidae?

facts.statement: The snout of Archaeornithoides features a long antorbital fenestra extending over three quarters of the maxilla's length.
facts.quote: El hocico de Archaeornithoides cuenta con una larga fenestra anteorbital, se extiende más de tres cuartas partes de la longitud del maxilar.

facts.statement: The generic name Archaeornithoides means "shaped like an ancient bird" in Ancient Greek, while the specific name deinosauriscus alludes to its small size.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico Archaeornithoides significa "con forma de ave antigua" en el antiguo griego, mientras que el epíteto específico A. deinosauriscus alude a su pequeño tamaño.

facts.statement: Elżanowski and Wellnhofer suggested in 1993 that Archaeornithoides was closely related to Avialae.
facts.quote: Elżanowski & Wellnhofer (1993) sugirieron que Archaeornithoides era un lo más cercano a Avialae.

facts.statement: The authors who described it in 1993 concluded that Archaeornithoides was closely related to troodontids, Spinosauridae, and Lisboasaurus.
facts.quote: Los autores que lo describieron en 1993 concluyeron que Archaeornithoides estaba estrechamente relacionado con los troodóntidos, Spinosauridae y Lisboasaurus

facts.statement: Later research rejected a close relationship between spinosaurids and troodontids and showed that Lisboasaurus is a crocodylomorph.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la investigación posterior ha no se admite una relación estrecha entre espinosáuridos y troodóntidos y más tarde se demostró que Lisboasaurus es un cocodrilomórfo.

facts.statement: Some scientists have suggested that the juvenile specimen of Archaeornithoides might belong to a previously known Mongolian species, such as the troodontids Saurornithoides or Byronosaurus.
facts.quote: Algunos científicos han sugerido que el espécimen juvenil de Archaeornithoides puede pertenecer a una especie conocida previamente en Mongolia, como los troodóntidos Saurornithoides o Byronosaurus.

facts.statement: Bever and Norell found no evidence to support placing Archaeornithoides near Avialae and only weak support for the idea that it is a juvenile troodontid.
facts.quote: Bever y Norell no encontró ninguna evidencia para apoyar la colocación de Archaeornithoides cerca de Avialae, y sólo un débil apoyo a la idea de que es un trodóntido juvenil.

facts.statement: The parent group of Archaeornithoides is Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Archaeornithoides belongs to the family Troodontidae.
facts.quote: Family: Troodontidae

facts.statement: Archaeornithoides is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Archaeornithoides lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Archaeornithoides was named by Elzanowski and Wellnhofer in 1992.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Archaeornithoides (genus), Elzanowski and Wellnhofer 1992
